title: The Best Interface Is the One You Forget
description: An essay arguing that the most successful design recedes from attention: when a tool works, people stop noticing it and only notice what they are doing with it.
body: A door handle you never think about is a triumph. The moment you notice it, something has gone wrong. Okafor walks through train station signage, kitchen knives and banking apps to argue that good design is measured by how little of it you register. Ornament asks for attention; craft gives attention back. The essay ends on a provocation: designers should be proud when no one remembers their work, only how easy the day felt.
note: This is the one I keep coming back to when people ask what good design is.

title: Make things, not throughput
body: Every app on my phone wants me to be efficient. None of them asks whether I made anything worth keeping this week. Output is not the same as making. The best weeks I've had were slow, wasteful, full of dead ends, and produced one thing I'm proud of. Measure the work by what it lets you imagine next, not by how fast it cleared the list.
context: Wrote this after the quarterly planning offsite.

title: Butternut squash & blush
caption: Two worn boards meeting edge to edge: dusty mauve-pink on top, scratched butternut orange-brown below, with the two colour names set in small white type.
ocr: butternut squash & blush
note: The light. Want something with this warmth for the packaging.
context: Used as a mood reference for the Harvest Co. packaging pitch.

title: On awakening
quote: The whole art of teaching is only the art of awakening the natural curiosity of young minds for the purpose of satisfying it afterwards.
note: For the workshop intro — teaching as lighting a fuse, not filling a bucket.

title: The Feedback Loop in Your Pocket
description: How the devices we design end up redesigning our habits: notifications, streaks and infinite feeds as quiet trainers of human behaviour.
body: We build tools to serve our intentions, then the tools start writing new intentions for us. Marchetti traces how a single red badge changed how millions of people check, wait, and feel. The argument is not that technology is bad but that every interface is a proposal about how a person should behave, and we accept those proposals without reading them.

title: Gardens, Not Streams
description: A case for treating the web as a place you tend over years rather than a feed that washes past you.
body: The stream is chronological and disposable: what matters is what's new. The garden is topological: what matters is what connects. Adeyemi argues that most of the web became a stream by accident and that personal sites, wikis and slow publishing are a way back to the garden. You don't finish a garden; you return to it.
note: This completely changed how I see the internet. I'd been treating everything like a feed.
context: Sent this to Maya after our walk about quitting social media.

title: The Magpie Method
description: On keeping a commonplace book: gathering fragments that catch your eye long before you know what they are for.
body: Magpies don't plan their nests in advance. They pick up what glitters and work out the architecture later. Grant describes thirty years of notebooks filled with ticket stubs, overheard sentences and diagrams, and how almost every project she finished began as something she had saved for no reason at all. Collecting without a purpose is not hoarding; it is giving your future self material.

title: Self-Reliance, on trusting your own thought
quote: A man should learn to detect and watch that gleam of light which flashes across his mind from within.

title: Sunset over the front page

ocr: The New York Times. All the News That's Fit to Print. Wednesday, December 3, 2025

title: High Lonesome perfume

ocr: High Lonesome by Mondo Mondo for Land. Mesquite dirt palo santo musk. California Mexico Texas

title: There Must Be More to Life Than This
description: From Anthony Gerace's series There Must Be More to Life Than This: found vintage material reconfigured into unique, abstract gridded collages. Gerace is a Canadian artist in London whose work is concerned with the effect of time on objects and images.
caption: A vintage photo of a woman in a white halter top against a blue sky, cut into a grid of squares with most of them replaced by flat blue, so she is only half there.

title: Episode 112 — Boredom is a doorway
description: A neuroscientist and a novelist talk about why unstructured, boring time is where new ideas form, and why filling every gap with input starves the mind.
note: The bit at 34 minutes about the 'default mode' — ideas need empty rooms.

title: Notes on Making
description: A slim book by a furniture maker on learning a craft by hand: patience, failure, and the way materials teach you if you let them.
note: Chapter 3 on 'letting the wood decide' is relevant to how we run design crits.

title: Highlight from Notes on Making
quote: The chair you design on paper is never the chair you build. The wood has opinions.

title: Why Your Calendar Is Not Your Life
description: A productivity coach on time blocking, inbox zero and squeezing more focus hours out of the week.
body: Block your mornings. Batch your email. Track every hour for two weeks and you will find at least six hours of waste. The most productive people treat their calendar as a budget and guard it ruthlessly.

title: Are.na channel: Unfinished buildings
description: A shared channel of photos of half-built concrete structures, rebar and scaffolding.

title: How a letterpress studio sets type
description: A ten-minute film of a printer setting metal type by hand, inking the press, and pulling the first proof.
note: The sound of it. Slowness as a feature.

title: Thoreau on simplicity
quote: Our life is frittered away by detail. Simplify, simplify.

title: Idea: a library that forgets on purpose
body: What if saved items slowly faded unless you touched them? Not deletion — more like a garden going to seed. The things you return to stay vivid. Might be a way to fight the guilt of an unread pile.

title: Children Are Scientists
description: Research summary on how toddlers form and test hypotheses through play, and why open-ended exploration beats instruction in early years.
body: Give a three-year-old a box with a hidden switch and watch. They will poke, predict, repeat and revise. Raman summarises a decade of studies showing that young children learn most when they are allowed to wonder and investigate on their own terms, and least when an adult tells them the answer first.

title: Sand Co. fabric swatch
caption: A scanned swatch of stretchy fabric printed with smudged animal-print blotches in black, chocolate and rust on cream, 'Sand Co.' written on it in blue biro.
ocr: Sand Co.

title: Taste Is a Muscle
description: On developing creative judgment by deliberately collecting, comparing and articulating why you like what you like.
body: Taste is not a gift you are born with. It is built by exposure and by naming. Park suggests keeping a swipe file and writing one sentence about each thing in it: why does this work? Over months the sentences become a point of view.

title: Highlight from The Magpie Method
quote: You cannot connect the dots you never collected.

title: Small Software
description: In praise of tools made by one person for a few hundred people, and what they get right that venture-funded apps don't.
body: Small software has a voice. It does one thing and admits it. It does not need to grow, so it does not need to manipulate you into staying. Adeyemi lists a dozen examples and argues for a web of workshops rather than malls.

title: Conversation with Dev about rituals
body: Dev said every creative practice he trusts has a ritual at the start: sharpening pencils, a walk, the same playlist. The ritual isn't superstition, it's a doorway that tells your body what's about to happen.
context: Coffee with Dev, after the conference.

title: William Morris on the useful and the beautiful
quote: Have nothing in your houses that you do not know to be useful, or believe to be beautiful.

title: The Attention Economy Was a Choice
description: A short history of ad-funded software and how engagement metrics became the default definition of success on the internet.
body: Nothing about the internet required it to optimise for time-on-site. That was a business decision, repeated until it looked like physics. Marchetti argues that if it was chosen, it can be unchosen.

title: Jolene, a love supreme
caption: A bakery's website on butter-yellow, framed in dark brown: a hand-drawn wordmark, a thin nav, and 'a Love Supreme' scrawled huge like a child wrote it, over a calm centred serif story.
ocr: Jolene. Locations Reservations Shop Stories Contact. a Love Supreme. We opened Primeur in 2014 in a beautiful old garage on the side of a leafy back street in Hackney

title: Episode 47 — The commonplace book
description: Two historians on Renaissance commonplace books, where readers copied passages under headings so they could reuse them in letters and speeches.

title: Essay draft: the case for wandering
body: Search is for when you know what you want. Wandering is for when you don't. Most tools only support the first. I want a way to browse my own past like a used bookshop: sorted just enough to stumble on something.
context: Opening paragraph for the newsletter essay, issue 14.

title: Plutarch on the mind
quote: The mind is not a vessel that needs filling but wood that needs igniting.

title: Ten Tools for Deep Work
description: A listicle of focus apps, website blockers, noise generators and time trackers.

title: Twelve squares of old magazines
caption: A three-by-four grid of squares cut from vintage magazines: a woman's face, a pink shoe, a car, flat squares of blue, green and orange, houndstooth, a smile.

title: Designing for the Second Visit
description: Most products are designed for first impressions. Okafor argues for designing for the hundredth use: calm, predictable, and quietly helpful.
body: Delight wears off. Reliability compounds. The second visit should feel like coming home, not like being sold to again.

title: Walk thought: ideas as compost
body: Old notes aren't dead, they're compost. Things I saved two years ago and forgot are now quietly feeding whatever I'm thinking about today. Maybe the point of saving isn't retrieval, it's digestion.

title: Colour palette generator from photos
description: A small web tool that extracts five dominant colours from any uploaded photograph.

title: The Library of Unread Books
description: Why a personal library full of books you haven't read is a map of your curiosity, not a record of failure.
body: The unread books are the point. They are a list of questions you have not answered yet. A library of only finished books is a trophy case.

title: Dewey on education
quote: Education is not an affair of telling and being told, but an active and constructive process.

title: Studio visit: a painter who works in series
description: A painter explains working on twenty canvases at once so that ideas jump between them, and why she never finishes one in isolation.

title: Your Phone Is a Slot Machine
description: Quick news piece on a study linking pull-to-refresh gestures with compulsive checking.

title: Pitch notes: Harvest Co.
body: Packaging should feel like late sun on clay. Earthy, warm, imperfect. Avoid anything glossy. Reference: kiln room photo, autumn market, the desert poster colours.

title: In Praise of Margins
description: White space on the page, slack in the schedule, idle hours in the week: why systems without margins break and people without margins stop having ideas.

title: Highlight from Gardens, Not Streams
quote: You don't finish a garden; you return to it.

title: Everyday makeup, on a loop
caption: A short looping video of an everyday makeup look being put on: soft skin, a little blush, a careful lip.

title: The Shape of a Conversation
description: A linguist on how good conversations wander, double back and build on half-finished thoughts, and why agendas kill them.

title: Remixing Is How Ideas Are Born
description: New ideas are mostly old ideas meeting for the first time. An essay on juxtaposition, collage and creative theft.
body: Put two things side by side that have never met and watch them argue. Collage artists, DJs and essayists all work the same way: they collect widely and then force strangers into the same room.

title: Online exhibition: Japanese packaging 1950–1970
description: A museum's online collection of mid-century Japanese product packaging: matchboxes, sweets, soap.

title: Thought after the workshop
body: The participants who asked the most questions made the most interesting things. Curiosity beat skill every single time. Next workshop: start with questions, not instructions.
context: Debrief from the April teaching workshop.

title: Speed Is Not a Strategy
description: A founder reflects on burning out while shipping features weekly, and on discovering that the work he is proudest of took the longest.
body: We shipped forty features in a year and I can't remember one of them. The thing customers still thank us for took nine slow months and a lot of staring out of the window.

title: Rilke on questions
quote: Be patient toward all that is unsolved in your heart and try to love the questions themselves.

title: dianthus_superbus_composition_022

title: How Search Forgot About Memory
description: Search engines match words; people remember feelings, places and moments. An essay on why personal search should work like recollection.
body: Nobody remembers a document by its filename. You remember where you were, who sent it, how it made you feel. Marchetti argues that personal tools should index those things too.

title: Reminder to self
body: Stop saving productivity listicles. They never help. Save the weird stuff.

title: The Shelf Life of Inspiration
description: Inspiration you save today often only becomes useful years later. Park on patience, archives and letting references ripen.

title: Design: The Definitive Visual History
description: A reference history of design through its designers, manufacturers, objects and movements, from Arts and Crafts and Art Nouveau through Art Deco and mid-century modern to the digital age. Timelines, catalogues of glassware, posters, typography and furniture, and profiles of William Morris, the Bauhaus, Alvar Aalto, Frank Lloyd Wright and Vitra.
note: The big orange 'des ign' cover is the best thing in the studio.

title: Grid systems in graphic design

title: Afterwords

title: Any Person Is the Only Self

note: Someone passed this along in Today and I bought my own copy.

title: Ex-Wife
